Vydrží mladým vyšší důvěra?: Will young people keep their higher trust?
Mladí v&nbsp;Česku (16&nbsp;až 29&nbsp;l: Young people in Czechia (aged 16 to 29) trust other people more than those aged 65 and over: 5.8 versus 5.0 on a scale of 0 to 10. The question is whether they lose that trust as they age or carry it with them. The catalogue therefore tracks the 25 to 34 age group: in 2025 it scored 5.5, the whole population aged 16 and over 5.3. In 2031 it will consist of people who were 19 to 28 in 2025.
průměr let 2029&nbsp;až 2031&nbsp;aspoň: 2029 to 2031 average of at least 5.7 and at least 0.3 points above the total: a signal in favour of a more trusting generation
průměr let 2029&nbsp;až 2031&nbsp;nejvýš: 2029 to 2031 average of at most 5.5, or a gap to the total of at most 0.2 points: a signal that young people’s higher trust may not last
Padne-li výsledek mezi obě budoucnosti,: If the result falls between the two futures, an honest “undecided” applies. The thresholds alone do not separate the effects of age, generation and period; they only show the direction. Today’s published values (5.5 and a gap of 0.2 points) would mean future B. But the test will be decided only by the 2029 to 2031 average.
Eurostat, EU-SILC 2025; prahy jsou hypot: Eurostat, EU-SILC 2025; the thresholds are catalogue hypotheses set in advance and will be evaluated from published rounded values once 2031 data are released; ages in 2031 are a derivation; comparison with 2013 (low reliability) suggests an age effect, the ESS survey a period effect (derivation)
Podíl investičních fondů na finančních ú: The share of investment funds in Czech households’ financial savings has roughly doubled in five years to 22%. But deposits still hold the majority, 57%.
Krize se dnes splétají: rychlý šok naraz: Crises now intertwine: a fast shock meets slow tension and one spills into the other. Some shocks are known in advance from risk registers, but turning warnings into preparedness is often missing.
Informace o penězích jsou zdarma. Zdarma: Information about money is free. What is not free is advice that someone stands behind and helps you carry through. The question is whether people will pay for it, or a free answer from AI will be enough.
Když AI zvedne produktivitu, někdo ten z: When AI raises productivity, someone gets the gain. We don’t know whether it will flow into wages, corporate profits or lower prices.
Poboček bank ubývá rychleji než jejich z: Bank branches are disappearing faster than their staff. We don’t know who will advise people about money: a banker, an AI assistant, or an influencer.
Vklady drží pojištění, důvěra a pohodlno: Deposits are held in place by insurance, trust and convenience. Instant payments, AI agents and new forms of money could make moving savings a matter of a few clicks.
Česko má proti průměru EU zhruba polovič: Czechia has roughly half the EU average debt (44% versus 82% of GDP in 2025). The problem is the deficit and ageing: debt would grow even if the state paid interest only at the rate of inflation.
První čínský šok Německo ustálo díky pro: Germany weathered the first China shock thanks to its links with Central Europe. The second targets this very chain: Chinese suppliers are replacing European ones inside European production.
Půjčka, pojistka i splátky se čím dál ča: Loans, insurance and instalments are increasingly offered right at the purchase, in an online shop or an app. Whoever owns the moment of payment owns the data and the customer relationship.
Snadné srovnání tlačí dolů ceny produktů: Easy comparison pushes down the prices of products that are simple to compare. Advice someone stands behind does not get cheaper this way, and companies resist comparison with opaque price lists.
Spojenci v NATO se zavázali dávat do rok: NATO allies have committed to spend 5% of GDP on defence and security by 2035, at least 3.5% of it on defence itself. Meanwhile cheap drones are changing the battlefield.
Evropa platí za energii trvale víc než U: Europe pays permanently more for energy than the US and China because it imports most of its oil and gas. Those who use less energy can turn this into an advantage.
Nevíme, jestli náklady na AI, bezpečnost: We don’t know whether only big players can carry the costs of AI, security and regulation, or whether AI will instead let small teams serve millions of people.
Digitální měny navázané na euro nebo dol: Digital currencies pegged to the euro or the dollar (stablecoins) could drain cheap deposits from banks, or become a new bank service. In Europe the second path prevails so far.
Evropská pravidla otevřela drobným inves: European rules have opened funds that invest outside the stock exchange to retail investors: the minimum investment and the cap on portfolio share are gone. We don’t know whether this will be an opportunity or a disappointment at the first downturn.
Nevíme, jestli se rovnovážná úroková saz: We don’t know whether the neutral interest rate will return to the low levels of the last decade after 2022 to 2026, or stay permanently higher because of investment in AI and defence and because of public debt.
Škody z přírodních katastrof rostou v Ev: Losses from natural disasters in Europe are growing faster than insurers cover them. The uninsured part falls on households, municipalities and the state.
Česko se otepluje rychleji, než se čekal: Czechia is warming faster than expected: 2024 was 2 °C warmer than the 1991 to 2020 normal. Buildings are not ready for the heat.
Od roku 2026 stát běžným vlastníkům rodi: From 2026, instead of a renovation grant, the state pays ordinary owners of family houses the interest on a loan of up to CZK 2 million. Renovation thus becomes a household financial decision.
Česko umí vyrábět složité věci, velkou č: Czechia can make complex things, but much of the value is captured by others. Exports rest on cars and on Germany, that is, on one industry and one neighbour.
Hormuz, Suez, tchajwanské čipy, nizozems: Hormuz, Suez, Taiwanese chips, the Dutch machines that make them, Chinese rare-earth refining: a few places hold a large part of the world economy and are turning into instruments of policy.
Podle ECB by sucho, jaké přichází jednou: According to the ECB, a drought of the kind that comes once in 25 years would threaten almost 15% of euro area output. Over a third of corporate loans go to sectors sensitive to water shortages.
Over a year, Czechia has enough electricity. What is missing is grid capacity for new sources, and from 2028 winter peaks may lack dispatchable capacity. Model results differ; the European assessment may overstate the risk.
Nevíme, jestli se Česko a eurozóna po en: We don’t know whether Czechia and the euro area will return to steady growth and inflation at target after the 2026 energy shock, or whether repeated shocks and weak growth will become the norm.
Firmy a domácnosti plánují podle pravide: Firms and households plan around rules that last decades: retirement age, taxes, climate targets. We don’t know whether they will hold or flip with every election.
AI může zrychlit jednotlivé úkoly. Kolik: AI can speed up individual tasks. How much it will add to the productivity of the whole Czech economy we don’t yet know.
Emisní povolenky pro paliva v budovách a: Emission allowances for fuels in buildings and transport are due to start in 2028. We don’t know whether the carbon price will rise gradually or jump after the delays.
Evropská pravidla pro finance se mění v: European rules for finance are changing in several areas at once, from rules for AI to the digital euro. Deadlines keep shifting.
Stát mění pravidla penzijního spoření: s: The state is changing pension savings rules: a fee cap, the end of the performance fee and a strategy that lowers risk with age. Yet a large share of savings sits in funds that do not beat inflation.
Nevíme, jestli poradci zůstanou placeni: We don’t know whether advisers will remain paid by commissions from financial firms, or whether direct payment by the client will prevail. The middle way is closest for now: commissions with stricter rules.
Evropa chce, aby si lidé mohli svá finan: Europe wants people to be able to move their financial data to another provider. We don’t know whether this will change the market or end up as a costly obligation that almost nobody uses.
Ve fázi spoření za lidi čím dál víc rozh: In the saving phase, a default strategy increasingly decides for people. We don’t know whether advice will be needed at least when savings move elsewhere and when the pension is paid out.
Eurozóna připravuje veřejné digitální pe: The euro area is preparing public digital money to be less dependent on international card companies. It could arrive in 2029 at the earliest, if the necessary legislation is agreed.
Nevíme, jestli budou velmoci soupeřit, a: We don’t know whether the great powers will compete but keep trading through third countries, or whether the world will split and energy shocks will become the normal state.
V roce 2028 čeká Česko další kolo ozdrav: In 2028, Czechia faces another round of budget repair. We don’t know who will pay for it or whether a new tax on selected sectors will come.
Česko plní tři ze čtyř kritérií pro přij: Czechia meets three of the four criteria for adopting the euro; what is missing is entry into the exchange rate mechanism, a kind of waiting room for the euro, which it does not apply for. The question is whether politics and the public will move.
Evropské státy připisují Rusku kampaň sa: European states attribute a campaign of sabotage and hybrid attacks to Russia. We don’t know whether it will stay below the threshold of open conflict.
Evropa má diagnózu své slabé konkurences: Europe has a diagnosis of its weak competitiveness and a list of remedies. We don’t know whether by 2031 it will complete the single market for services and capital, or stop at the diagnosis.
Úmrtí bude v Česku přibývat a odchází ge: Deaths in Czechia will increase, and the generation that acquired flats and houses after 1989 is passing on. The first big wave of inherited housing lies ahead.
Česko patří v EU k zemím s nejrovnějšími: Czechia has some of the most equal incomes in the EU. Wealth, however, is distributed much more unequally, and flats are getting dearer faster than wages.
Internetové bankovnictví používá 85 % Če: 85% of Czechs aged 16 to 74 use internet banking. But money gets explained elsewhere, for young people often on social media.
Nevíme, kam se posunou lidé, kteří dnes: We don’t know where people who struggle with money today, or leave it lying idle, will move: to a plan with an adviser, to resignation, or to deciding on their own through apps.
AI umožní influencerovi mluvit vlastní t: AI will let an influencer talk to millions of people at once with their own face and voice. We don’t know whether this will become a new way of selling financial products or just a short episode.
Evropa poprvé navrhuje regulovat to, jak: For the first time, Europe proposes regulating how apps hold children’s attention: age limits and restrictions on infinite scrolling. Whether the measures will work we don’t yet know.
Češi nevěří všem institucím stejně: někt: Czechs don’t trust all institutions equally: some are trusted by most people, others by almost no one. We know where things stand today, not where they are heading.
Bydlení v Česku zdražuje rychleji než mz: Housing in Czechia is getting dearer faster than wages and is moving to the centre of political debate. So far, policy responds mainly by supporting demand.
Většina Čechů považuje dezinformace za v: Most Czechs see disinformation as a serious problem, yet only a minority trusts the news. We agree that lies do harm and argue about who may define them.
Výzkum potvrzuje, že lidé s vysokými pří: Research confirms that people with high incomes and weak ties to a place move for lower taxes. Figures on a record exodus of millionaires, however, are disputed.
Podle prvních studií z USA se v profesíc: According to first studies from the US, professions exposed to AI are hiring fewer beginners. In Czechia it is a warning for now: who will train the experienced people of 2035?
Řádné starobní důchody ukončené v roce 2: Regular old-age pensions that ended in 2024 had been drawn for almost 25 years on average, compared with 11 years in 1970. This is not an estimate for today’s new pensioners.
Zemřelých je v Česku víc než narozených: Czechia has more deaths than births, and the population holds up only thanks to immigration. Foreigners are gradually settling and becoming a large group of customers and colleagues.
Pokusy ukazují obojí: po AI, která rovno: Experiments show both: after AI that simply hands out answers, pupils do worse in a test without help; with AI designed as a tutor they learn faster. We don’t know which version will prevail.
Kdo vyrůstal v době rychlého růstu, věří: Those who grew up in times of rapid growth tend to believe the pie is growing. Today’s young Czechs have seen both the rapid catch-up with the West and its stalling, and we don’t know what they will take from it.
V roce 2025 se v Česku narodilo 77,6 tis: In 2025, 77,600 children were born in Czechia. Today there are 32 seniors for every 100 people aged 15 to 64; by 2050 the projection puts it at 47.
Velkou část péče podle odhadů zajišťují: According to estimates, a large part of care is provided by relatives. The state pays allowances, but Czechia has few long-term care workers compared with other advanced countries.
Naděje dožití v Česku byla v roce 2024 8: Life expectancy in Czechia was 80.1 years in 2024, of which 62.4 years in good health. Between 2010 and 2024 life expectancy rose, but the number of years without limitations in everyday activities fell.
Severozápad Čech měl v roce 2000 HDP na: In 2000, North-West Bohemia had GDP per capita in purchasing power parity at 61% of the EU average, and in 2024 again 61%. Poland’s Lublin region meanwhile moved from 35 to 55%. The 2024 figure for Lublin is preliminary; the Polish series has breaks.
Mladí Češi věří druhým lidem víc než ti: Young Czechs trust other people more than older ones: 5.8 versus 5.0 on a scale of 0 to 10. We don’t know whether they will carry that trust as they age or lose it, with distrust continuing to hold back investment and enterprise.
Výsledky českých žáků souvisejí s rodinn: Czech pupils’ results are more strongly linked to family background than is usual in the OECD. Among adults, too, the use of AI and further learning differ by level of education.
Porodnost v Česku za pár let prudce kles: Fertility in Czechia fell sharply within a few years, to 1.28 children per woman in 2025. We don’t know whether this is postponement or the start of permanently smaller families.
Odborná odpověď od AI rychle zlevňuje. R: An expert answer from AI is quickly getting cheaper. Advice someone stands behind is not, and services in Czechia have long been getting dearer faster than goods.
Lidé se na peníze začínají ptát AI dřív,: People are starting to ask AI about money before they go to the bank. Its advice tends to be sensible, but not equally good for everyone.
České domácnosti drží 3,4 bilionu korun: Czech households hold CZK 3.4 trillion in demand deposits and CZK 0.94 trillion in term deposits, even though the latter earn more. Easier comparison and AI agents could weaken this convenience.
Technika pro platby, které za člověka za: The technology for payments that an AI agent makes on a person’s behalf is developing faster than people’s interest. Nobody has yet determined who is liable for a wrong purchase.
Každý osmý trestný čin v Česku se dnes p: Every eighth crime in Czechia is now committed online. Faking a message, a voice or a face is cheap; verifying authenticity is not.
Když poradí stroj a rada selže, kdo nese: When a machine gives advice and the advice fails, who bears the loss? A licensed institution that stands behind it, or a free AI with no guarantee?
Telefon a vyhledávač vědí, co člověk chy: The phone and the search engine know what a person is planning weeks before their bank sees it. We don’t know whether the rules will level this advantage.
Finance patří k hlavním trhům tvůrců vel: Finance is among the main markets for the makers of large language models. The catalogue tracks above all the combination of a general model with data and agents for specific work.
K nové technologii se dnes dostanou skor: Almost all countries now get access to a new technology at roughly the same time. They differ in how fully they use it, and that is a matter of how companies are managed.
Evropská rada pro systémová rizika poprv: For the first time, the European Systemic Risk Board has called cyber risk to the financial system as a whole serious. One attacked firm can be absorbed; it is worse when shared software hits many institutions at once.
Nikdo neví, kdy kvantový počítač prolomí: Nobody knows when a quantum computer will break today’s encryption. But authorities have already set deadlines for moving to new methods, for critical infrastructure in the EU by the end of 2030.
Podvodů přibývá a otázka je, komu lidé s: Fraud is increasing, and the question is whom people will entrust with verifying authenticity: a bank, a tech platform, or the state with a digital identity.
Špičková AI vzniká v USA a v Číně. Nevím: Frontier AI is being built in the US and China. We don’t know whether Europe will build its own or remain a smart user of other people’s models.
Datová centra pro AI se čím dál víc stav: Data centres for AI are increasingly built on debt. We don’t know whether revenues will grow before creditors run out of patience, and who will bear any loss.
AI může šetřit čas při jednotlivých úkol: AI can save time on individual tasks. The catalogue’s hypothesis is that a bigger benefit for a company requires redesigning the work.
V českém zpracovatelském průmyslu pracuj: 24% of employed people in Czechia work in manufacturing, the most in the EU. The question here is not whether robots will come, but whether they will help keep production in a country where labour is getting dearer and scarcer.
